citeAs: Awadalla, A., Xue, L., Lo, O., Shu, M., Lee, H., Guha, E., Jordan, M., Shen, S., Awadalla, M., Savarese, S., Xiong, C., Xu, R., Choi, Y., Schmidt, L. (2024). MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv:2406.11271.
creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt (University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of California Berkeley)
description: MINT-1T-PDF-CC-2024-18 is the PDF subset of MINT-1T, a large-scale open-source multimodal interleaved dataset. PDF documents are sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files and parsed using PyMuPDF to extract interleaved sequences of images and text. The PDF subset contributes 93 billion text tokens to the overall MINT-1T dataset of one trillion tokens and 3.4 billion images.
name: MINT-1T-PDF-CC-2024-18
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation was performed. The data collection and labeling process was entirely automated using rule-based heuristics and deduplication methods. No crowdworkers or contractors were involved.
rai:dataBiases: The PDF subset shows a higher proportion of Science and Technology documents compared to other subsets. The paper avoids model-based text quality classifiers as they have been shown to favor text from certain demographics. The dataset may contain content from the public web that reflects societal biases.
rai:dataCollection: PDF documents are sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files from February 2023 to April 2024 dumps. PDF links are extracted from these dumps, then downloaded and read using PyMuPDF. Documents larger than 50MB or over 50 pages are discarded. Reading order is extracted by finding bounding boxes of text blocks, clustering by columns, and ordering top-left to bottom-right. Images are anchored based on proximity to text blocks.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF documents sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files. For PDFs, the dataset releases the text along with the URL for the PDF and a list of image reference numbers used to parse the images from the documents.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data collected from January 2024 to June 2024. PDF source documents from CommonCrawl WAT files span February 2023 to April 2024 dumps.
rai:dataLimitations: PDF parsing has two known limitations: (1) sometimes unable to detect images; (2) incorrect reading order extraction due to arbitrary PDF layouts (e.g., reading across column boundaries). The dataset is not self-contained and relies on downloading external image URLs, with no guarantee these URLs will remain available over time (link rot). The dataset may contain confidential or sensitive content from the public web despite filtering efforts.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For PDF documents, images with aspect ratio greater than 3 are removed (to preserve scientific figures while filtering low-quality images). Images smaller than 150 pixels or larger than 20,000 pixels are removed. Documents containing any NSFW image are discarded entirely. Paragraph deduplication removes documents where more than 80% of paragraphs are duplicates. Images appearing more than ten times within a snapshot are removed via SHA256 hash deduplication.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents undergo: (1) discarding PDFs over 50MB or 50 pages; (2) excluding pages with no text; (3) reading order extraction via bounding box clustering; (4) non-English document removal using FastText language identification (threshold 0.65); (5) removal of documents with URLs containing NSFW substrings; (6) text quality filtering using RefinedWeb methods (duplicate n-grams, MassiveText rules); (7) image filtering removing images smaller than 150px or larger than 20,000px, and aspect ratio greater than 3; (8) NSFW image detection; (9) PII removal (email and IP address masking); (10) paragraph and document deduplication using Bloom Filter; (11) image deduplication via SHA256 hashes.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be distributed as JSON shards through the HuggingFace interface. Authors will actively respond to issues and maintain the dataset. Updates will be communicated through the README on the HuggingFace dataset page. Older versions can be found using Git history. A Google form will be provided for opting data out of MINT-1T. Contributions can be made through the Pull Request mechanism of the HuggingFace interface.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MINT-1T aims to democratize multimodal AI research by providing a large-scale open-source dataset, bridging the gap between open and closed-source models. The dataset includes safety filtering to remove NSFW content and PII. Using the dataset to train models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or for military applications is considered inappropriate.
rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training large multimodal models that process interleaved images and text sequences. Additional use cases include generating interleaved image and text sequences, and building multimodal document retrieval systems. Not appropriate for training models that ingest or generate personally identifying information or for military applications.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: FastText language identification model (confidence threshold 0.65) for non-English document removal; NSFW image detector for pornographic content removal; GPT-2 tokenizer used to calculate number of text tokens for analysis; PyMuPDF for PDF parsing; Bloom Filter for text deduplication; SHA256 hashing for image deduplication.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset may contain personally identifiable information (PII) from the public web, including images of individuals and text about specific individuals. Email addresses and IP addresses are masked. The dataset may also contain sensitive data such as race/ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, financial or health data if present on the public web.
